structured_output.hypothesis: Among cones of one conifer species sharing a given parastichy pair (e.g. 5:8 in Norway spruce), the share with the major series running right-handed is statistically indistinguishable from 50%.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In a pooled sample of at least 400 same-species cones with the same parastichy pair and a recorded handedness, the right-handed fraction lies within 0.45 to 0.55, and a two-sided exact binomial test against p=0.5 gives p>0.05. For the quoted case, 224 of 467 is 0.480, so p is about 0.3.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The right-handed fraction is below 0.45 or above 0.55, or the two-sided exact binomial test against p=0.5 gives p<0.01, in a same-species, same-arrangement sample of at least 400 cones.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's "direction" is the handedness of the spiral series, such as the five-series, read on the cone surface. A modern dataset would record the chirality of the dominant or ontogenetic parastichy per cone, or the clockwise and anticlockwise parastichy counts per cone. The match is exact only for per-cone handedness together with a parastichy pair, and only for cones of one species. Clockwise and anticlockwise counts alone give handedness only if the convention for which series is the 5-series is stated.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I found no public dataset of per-cone parastichy handedness for Norway spruce or any other extant conifer. Two rounds of searching (Dryad, Zenodo, figshare) turned up only journal papers that report handedness counts in their text, such as studies of slash pine, lodgepole pine and black pine. The one deposit-like lead, Araucaria mirabilis cone parastichy counts, concerns Middle Jurassic fossil cones, not an extant species, so it falls outside the claim's scope of cones of one species. I could not confirm that a data deposit exists for it. I did not fetch any dataset landing page, so I name none rather than risk an unverified identifier. The claim could be tested only by new counts or by digitising the tables in the published papers.
